Outside the proposed scope but the same fault and fix: 3 matches (6 rows) that Stage 0 drops only for B6 and that pass every check after the fix, and Doha's SF and F rows (4, MCP-confirmed); listed in f1_extension_rows.csv, not voted here.

F2.scope: 58 of the 88 matches (116 player rows): 55 where an independent record holds each player's counts on the other player's row (WTA API 52: Abu Dhabi 2021 all 28, Phillip Island 2021 all 18, San Jose 2022, Linz 2023 Q2, Hua Hin 2024, Charleston 2024, Saint-Malo 2025 x2; US Open official statistics: US Open 2022 Q1 Seppi-Horansky; Wimbledon official statistics and Slam point-by-point: Wimbledon 2019 R128 Wang-Martincova; ATP Infosys key statistics: Miami 2025 R64 Bergs-Rublev) and 3 on internal evidence alone (Roanne CH 2021 R32 Debru-Pellegrino, Barletta CH 2025 R16 Dodig-Sultanov, W50 Indian Harbour Beach 2025 R32 Karatancheva-Kononova). The other 30 are rejected; f2_matches.csv gives all 88 with verdict and reason.
F2.fix: Exchange all nine counts between the two players of each listed match (Sackmann raw w_* <-> l_* of the listed _source_file/_row).
F2.reasons: Confirmed with a record: the WTA API equals the exchanged box on all 9 counts for both players (18/18) in each of the 52 WTA matches, and its result string names the recorded winner with the same score; US Open 2022 Q1: the official statistics equal the exchanged box on 16/16 counts (TML, a different source, 15/18); Wimbledon 2019: the official statistics and Sackmann's Slam point-by-point equal the exchanged box (Martincova exactly; Wang within one point); Miami 2025: the ATP's own key statistics for Bergs equal the box recorded under Rublev on 7/7 rates and its total-points share fits the box under Bergs; Sofascore disagrees with both boxes there. Every exchanged box passes B0-B9 and every recorded winner advanced or is the record's winner. Residual in 2 confirmed matches (Wimbledon 2019, US Open 2022 Q1): Sackmann's service-game count is one short for one player; the exchange moves that one-game error to the other player and fixes the other 8 counts. Confirmed internally: no record, but as recorded each player's box gives the OTHER player's games (identity off by 5, 5 and 9 games), B != 0 and D != 0 so neither an exchange of service games alone nor of break points alone explains it, the exchange makes the identity exact for both players and turns the points from 82-97, 48-58, 29-56 to the winner's side (29 points cannot win 6-2 6-1), and the winner advanced; the same pattern occurs in 18 refereed matches and the record confirmed the exchange in all 18 (all 51 refereed matches with an identity miss of 3+ games were exchanges). Rejected (30): 7 where a record shows the box AS RECORDED, so the exchange would corrupt it: AO 2012 R32 Kukushkin-Monfils and Wimbledon 2016 R128 Bellucci-Bemelmans (Slam point-by-point), AO 2022 Q1 De Vroome-Radwanska (MCP 16/16), AO 2022 R128 Paire-Monteiro (Sofascore), Palermo 2022 R32 Sorribes Tormo-Bogdan (WTA API 18/18), AO 2025 Q2 Garin-Djere and AO 2025 R128 Blinkova-Saville (AO official point-by-point); in several only the service games are exchanged. All 7 have B = 0, where the identity cannot tell a whole-box exchange from a service-games exchange; of the 8 refereed B = 0 matches 7 are as recorded. 23 have no record and ambiguous evidence: B = 0 (18, incl. every Davis Cup / Fed Cup rubber), an identity miss of one game (3), the exchanged box still failing the identity (Antalya, Tenerife), and the W35 Timaru final, whose raw row (score 1-6 2-6, box giving the 'winner' 3 games) is consistent with the recorded winner having LOST: the winner label, not the box, may be wrong. The audit's one-sided identity test passes Palermo and the two residual cases; the two-sided test used here does not.
checks: Independent records searched per match: WTA API, MCP, Sackmann Slam point-by-point, US Open and Wimbledon official statistics, AO/RG Infosys point-by-point and key statistics, ATP Infosys key statistics 2025, Sofascore, Tennislive, TDI, and TML's copy (f2_referee_rows.csv)

Simulation of the exchange: B0-B9 pass on all 88 (replica equals stage0_build.box_scores); games identity on BOTH players exact for 56 of the 58 confirmed (2 residual one-game service-game misses)
Minimum-points rule (4 points per game won, 7 per tiebreak): as recorded it fails in 22 matches, after the exchange in none
Progression: the recorded winner plays a later round in every confirmed match without a WTA API result string (6); 11 of the 30 rejected are finals or team rubbers with no later round
TML holds 63 of the 88 and equals Sackmann's row (16-18 of 18 counts) in 61, so it is a copy and not used as a referee; where it differs (US Open 2022 Q1) it backs the exchange

F5.fix: Not confirmed: whole-box replacement by counts derived from RG's key statistics.
F5.reasons: The fault is real and the official numbers are right where they differ: RG's key statistics equal RG's own point-by-point on 99.3-99.95% of player rows for svpt, aces, double faults, first serves in and first- and second-serve points won; in Sackmann's rows with extra first serves the moved points were won 51.8% (men's qualifying), 47.6% (women's), 53.3% / 45.8% (main draws), second-serve rates; MCP, independent, backs the key statistics over Sackmann in 79.5% vs 5.1% of disputed first-in rows and 100% vs 0% of disputed serve-point rows. Sofascore equals Sackmann at RG 2022-25 on 95.5-100% of rows, so it is the same faulty source, not a referee. But the proposed fix is not clear: (1) the key statistics do not give service games; derived from the opponent's 'Break Points Converted Games' denominator, the two players' total equals the games played in 416 of 467 matches and exceeds it by 1-3 in 51, and it equals Sackmann's service games in only 68% (men's main draw) and 84% (women's) of rows; with it the games identity holds in 325 of 455 matches; (2) unlike Wimbledon and the US Open, the feed cannot be shown to match Sackmann's measurement on clean rows: no clean RG overlap exists (the 2025 main draw itself has the fault in about 19% of rows and its svpt differs in 6-8%); aces and break points do match 100%; (3) the 6 Oct decision lists Sackmann's RG men's qualifying 2022-2025 under 'Not decided', 'left unchanged until a study measures its effect': not a bar on paper, but changing 2025 alone while F6 leaves 2022-24 as they are pre-empts that study and mixes conventions across seasons. A narrower fix (eight point counts from the key statistics, service games from RG's point-by-point under Sackmann's tiebreak convention) looks supportable but is a different operation and needs the owner's call.

F6.reasons: The fault is shown at the edition level, not per match: no official RG feed is held for 2022-24; Sofascore equals Sackmann at RG 2022-24 on 95.5-100% of rows (same source, not a referee); MCP charts only part of each draw (RG main draws 36-82 rows a year, qualifying 2-6) and agrees with Sackmann on first serves in in 37-64% of RG rows against 65-93% at the AO of the same years, which confirms the fault but is a hand chart, not a per-match official record; the Olympics have 72 MCP rows.
